site.name: Navish Kumar
site.statement: I study how learning systems remain reliable when mathematical assumptions, noisy data, and deployment constraints pull in different directions.
site.context: The portfolio is organized as a chain of arguments: formal structure, measurable systems, and decisions that matter in real settings.

principles.title: Think in Structure
principles.text: Start from invariants, failure modes, and geometry so the problem is defined by what must remain true, not by convenient heuristics.

principles.title: Build for Measurement
principles.text: Convert ideas into datasets, pipelines, and evaluation loops that expose whether a method actually behaves as intended.

principles.title: Link Theory to Decisions
principles.text: Treat proofs and models as decision tools: they should change how one allocates effort, risk, and resources in practice.

arcs.name: Mathematical Structure for Reliable Learning
arcs.thesis: Use spectral and geometric structure to derive guarantees for complex learning dynamics.
arcs.methods: Spectral graph theory, variational optimization, convergence analysis
arcs.practice: Sharper guarantees reduce fragile optimization behavior and improve confidence in model updates.

arcs.name: Data-Driven Urban Logistics
arcs.thesis: Model city context at micro-region level so sustainability transitions become operationally testable.
arcs.methods: H3 spatial indexing, OpenStreetMap aggregation, predictive service-time modeling
arcs.practice: Supports route-planning and fleet-transition choices for cargo-bike adoption.

arcs.name: Social Interaction and Counterspeech
arcs.thesis: Study how antagonistic and protective speech behaviors evolve in online communities.
arcs.methods: Dataset construction, lexical and psycholinguistic analysis, interaction modeling
arcs.practice: Informs moderation and intervention strategies beyond blunt account suspension.

timeline.title: Behavioral dynamics in adversarial online discourse
timeline.note: Established an empirical baseline through a paired hate/counter dataset and behavior analysis.

timeline.title: Normalized Laplacians for gain graphs
timeline.note: Shifted toward structural analysis, linking balance properties to spectral behavior.

timeline.title: Extremal eigenvalue bounds in gain Laplacians
timeline.note: Extended the spectral program with concrete lower and upper bounds tied to graph frustration.

timeline.title: Urban micro-region delivery modeling
timeline.note: Applied model-building to operational sustainability questions in last-mile logistics.

timeline.title: Optimization guarantees for natural-gradient variational inference
timeline.note: Unified practical optimization behavior with formal guarantees under a square-root covariance geometry.

08ZZubdj9fEC.summary: Provides convergence guarantees for natural-gradient variational Gaussian inference by using a square-root covariance parameterization.
08ZZubdj9fEC.contribution: Bridges an important theory-practice gap: methods known to work well empirically now come with provable behavior under concave likelihood settings.
08ZZubdj9fEC.build: Derives both discrete optimization and continuous-time flow guarantees, then validates behavior against Euclidean and Wasserstein baselines.
08ZZubdj9fEC.impact: Improves trust in natural-gradient VI for high-stakes modeling workflows where instability is costly.
08ZZubdj9fEC.timeline_note: Formalized why natural-gradient updates can be both fast and stable.

738O_yMBCRsC.summary: Models delivery performance by urban micro-region to estimate where cargo-bike logistics can replace polluting van fleets.
738O_yMBCRsC.contribution: Introduces datasets and a context-aware modeling setup that makes sustainability transitions measurable rather than aspirational.
738O_yMBCRsC.build: Combines Uber H3 geospatial partitioning with OpenStreetMap features to predict service-time components by neighborhood.
738O_yMBCRsC.impact: Enables operators and cities to evaluate low-emission last-mile strategies with operational evidence.
738O_yMBCRsC.timeline_note: Translated modeling work into an operational decision framework for real logistics systems.

WbkHhVStYXYC.summary: Derives lower and upper bounds for extremal eigenvalues of gain Laplacian matrices and links them to frustration measures.
WbkHhVStYXYC.contribution: Extends spectral guarantees beyond signed graphs and clarifies how structural imbalance governs stability-related eigenvalues.
WbkHhVStYXYC.build: Develops proofs that connect graph deletion notions (frustration number/index) to explicit Laplacian spectral bounds.
WbkHhVStYXYC.impact: Strengthens spectral tools for analyzing stability in signed and gain-network models.
WbkHhVStYXYC.timeline_note: Turned structural intuition into explicit, reusable spectral bounds.

OU6Ihb5iCvQC.summary: Introduces normalized Laplacians for gain graphs and studies their spectral properties, including balance and bipartiteness relationships.
OU6Ihb5iCvQC.contribution: Builds foundational definitions and interlacing extensions needed for later gain-graph spectral results.
OU6Ihb5iCvQC.build: Constructs the normalized operator framework, then proves bounds and characterizes equality cases.
OU6Ihb5iCvQC.impact: Provides a base layer for principled analysis of complex-unit gain networks.
OU6Ihb5iCvQC.timeline_note: Established the normalized operator framework that later bounds build upon.

SP6oXDckpogC.summary: Analyzes interaction dynamics between hate and counter users on Twitter using a curated paired-user dataset.
SP6oXDckpogC.contribution: Shows asymmetries in behavior, sentiment, and strategy, and demonstrates that counterspeech patterns vary by targeted community.
SP6oXDckpogC.build: Releases an annotated hate/counter account-pair dataset and applies lexical, linguistic, and psycholinguistic analyses.
SP6oXDckpogC.impact: Provides evidence for moderation strategies that preserve speech while reducing harm.
SP6oXDckpogC.timeline_note: Started from measurable social harm dynamics before moving deeper into formal structure and optimization.
